//: VITE RESOLVES A TSCONFIG PER FILE AND THE NEAREST ONE WINS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM. apps/portal/tsconfig.json sets `jsx: preserve` under ADR-095 F7, and that is correct for the application: tsconfig.base.json's rule is that nothing here is built by `tsc`, so Next emits and `tsc --noEmit` only reads. VITEST HAS NO BUNDLER BEHIND IT: it hands a module to Node, so preserved JSX reaches the import analyser as invalid syntax and the suite fails to load before one assertion runs. Vite names the cause itself: "Failed to parse source for import analysis because the content contains invalid JS syntax. If you use tsconfig.json, make sure to not set jsx to preserve." This file overrides `jsx` for THIS DIRECTORY ONLY, so the app keeps the setting its build needs and the suite gets JavaScript. It is deliberately NOT a root-level `esbuild` block in vitest.config.ts: that was tried and measured, and Vite reads the per-file tsconfig in preference, so a block there is configuration that looks like it works and does not. `tsc` never reads this file, because it compiles the project it is pointed at; Next never reads it either.
